sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: This is one of those modules that most ERPs underestimate.
A modern ERP without a proper document system becomes chaos.
Nobody knows which one is the latest.
We're building the enterprise knowledge layer.

sections.title: Phase 7 — Document Management
paragraphs: Every module we've built already needs it.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: A Document is not a File.
Business information represented by one or more files.

sections.title: A Document is a managed business record that stores structured metadata, version history, access controls, and one or more associated files while maintaining relationships to business entities throughout the ERP.
Responsibilities
paragraphs: It does not store binary content directly.

sections.title: Relationships
paragraphs: One of the most reusable entities.

sections.title: Search
paragraphs: This becomes one of the most-used searches in the ERP.

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: "The uploaded agreement differs from Version 3 by changes to payment terms and warranty clauses."
lists: Find all contracts for Vendor X.

sections.title: Document as the Enterprise Knowledge Hub
Engineering Summary
lists: The information foundation of the ERP.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: The business entities do not own the documents.
Instead, the Document Management module provides a shared repository that every other module can reference.
That eliminates duplication, keeps version history centralized, and gives the entire ERP a single source of truth for business documents.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would not allow direct uploads to the Document entity.
lists: Every uploaded file belongs to a version.
Every version belongs to one document.
The "current version" is simply a pointer.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next entity should be Document Version.
Versioning is what transforms a simple file repository into a true enterprise document management system.

With Document Version, KoreVity gains enterprise-grade document control similar to SharePoint, OpenText, or Documentum while remaining tightly integrated with every business module we've already built.
Now we build the entity that separates a good ERP from an enterprise ERP.
Every change becomes part of permanent business history.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: A Version is not a Document.
One specific revision of that record.

sections.title: A Document Version is an immutable snapshot of a document at a specific point in time, containing the associated file, metadata, author, approval status, and revision history.
Purpose
paragraphs: Document Versions become the foundation for:

sections.title: Responsibilities
paragraphs: It does not own the document.

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: "Version 6 introduces a new termination clause and extends payment terms from 30 to 45 days."
lists: What changed between Version 4 and Version 5?

sections.title: File Metadata Lives Here
paragraphs: Because each version has a different file.

sections.title: Document Version as the Revision Hub
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: Document Version is not a document.
lists: The version-control foundation of the ERP.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: The document model now mirrors source control systems.
This makes document history permanent, searchable, auditable, and AI-comparable.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: Rather than allowing version numbers to be typed manually, I'd support an automatic versioning strategy.
This is especially valuable for engineering drawings, policies, technical specifications, and controlled documentation.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next entity should be Stored File.
The final piece is the actual binary object.
By introducing Stored File as its own infrastructure entity, KoreVity can support:
without changing the business document model.
That clean separation is what makes enterprise document platforms highly scalable.
Now we reach one of the most important infrastructure entities in the entire ERP.
That creates duplication, inconsistent security, and migration nightmares.
We're going to solve it once.
lists: Cloud object storage (AWS S3, Azure Blob, Google Cloud Storage)

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: A Stored File is not a Document.
A Stored File is not a Version.

sections.title: A binary object stored by the platform.

A Stored File is the physical binary object managed by the platform, containing storage metadata, integrity information, security details, and storage-provider references independent of business entities.
Purpose
paragraphs: Stored Files become the foundation for:

sections.title: Responsibilities
paragraphs: It does not know anything about Customers, Projects, or Employees.

sections.title: Relationships
paragraphs: Stored File is referenced by many things.

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: AI now has secure access to file infrastructure.
AI works against Stored Files while business logic stays with Documents.

sections.title: Deduplicate Files
paragraphs: Three departments upload the exact same PDF.

sections.title: Storage Providers Should Be Replaceable
paragraphs: Tomorrow you can migrate to Azure without changing any business entities.

sections.title: Stored File as the Binary Infrastructure
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: Stored File is not a document.
lists: The file infrastructure of the ERP.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: At this point we've completely separated business information from storage.
All without changing a single business entity.
That's exactly the kind of clean architecture used in enterprise content management systems.
lists: Move from local storage to AWS S3.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I'd also support multiple storage classes.
The Stored File record stays the same, while the storage engine transparently moves the binary object between storage tiers to reduce infrastructure costs.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The final entity for Document Management should be Entity Link.

sections.title: Which business records use this document?
paragraphs: A generic Entity Link will allow any module—CRM, Sales, Procurement, HR, Assets, Projects, Service, Finance, or future modules—to attach documents without adding document-specific fields or tables, making the entire ERP truly modular.
This is the final entity of the entire Document Management module.
Ironically, it's also one of the most important architectural decisions in the entire ERP.
You'll end up with 80 attachment tables.
We're not going to do that.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: A Document does not belong to a Customer.
A Customer simply references a Document.
That same document may also belong to:

sections.title: An Entity Link is a generic association between a managed document and any business entity within the ERP, enabling reusable document relationships without module-specific attachment implementations.
Purpose
paragraphs: Entity Links become the foundation for:

sections.title: Responsibilities
paragraphs: It does not own the document.

sections.title: Relationships
paragraphs: This is one of the most reusable entities in KoreVity.

sections.title: Business Rules
paragraphs: Removing a link never deletes the document.

sections.title: Permissions
paragraphs: Usually inherited from the target entity.

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: This is where AI becomes incredibly powerful.
Show me everything related to Project Alpha.
AI instantly has complete project context.

sections.title: Entity Link as the Knowledge Network
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: Entity Link is not an attachment.
lists: The relationship foundation of Document Management.

sections.title: 🏛️ What We've Built
paragraphs: This is now a true enterprise document platform.
Every business module shares the same document infrastructure.

sections.title: One Architectural Refinement
paragraphs: I'd add a Relationship Scope field in a future enhancement.
This would allow the same document to be visible only within its intended business context without creating duplicate copies or special-case logic in each module.

sections.title: Overall Progress
paragraphs: You now have 58 core entities forming a coherent enterprise architecture.
The major business domains are complete:
These are not isolated modules—they are interconnected through consistent patterns: reference data, business events, permissions, audit trails, AI context, and reusable relationships.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next phase should be Workflow & Business Process Automation.
This is the point where KoreVity evolves from a system that stores business data into one that runs the business.

Approvals, notifications, escalations, automation rules, scheduled jobs, business workflows, and AI-assisted process orchestration can all be built as shared platform capabilities used by every module you've already designed.
This is the natural next step toward an enterprise-grade intelligent ERP.
Now we leave the world of business data and enter the world of business behavior.
Everything we've built so far stores information.
Now we're going to make the ERP do work automatically.
This is where KoreVity starts becoming an intelligent enterprise platform rather than just a database.

sections.title: Phase 8 — Workflow & Business Process Automation
paragraphs: Instead of every module building its own approval system...

sections.title: Phase Architecture
paragraphs: This phase doesn't belong to HR.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: A Workflow is not an Approval.
Approval is only one kind of workflow.

sections.title: A Workflow is a reusable business process definition that specifies the sequence of activities, decisions, participants, and automation required to complete a business operation.
Responsibilities
paragraphs: That will be handled later by Workflow Instance.

sections.title: Version
paragraphs: Instances always use the version they started with.

sections.title: Business Rules
paragraphs: Only one active version of the same workflow.

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: "Purchase Order approvals spend 82% of their time waiting for finance approval. Consider parallel approvals."
This is exactly where AI delivers operational value.
lists: Which workflows are failing most often?

sections.title: Version Everything
paragraphs: New ones use the latest version.

sections.title: Engineering Summary
lists: The process foundation of the ERP.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: This is the first entity that doesn't belong to a business department.
It belongs to the platform itself.
Every module will use the same engine.
Instead of every module reinventing the wheel.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: Common logic is inherited while allowing module-specific customization.
This keeps workflow maintenance manageable as the ERP grows.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next entity should be Workflow Step.
A workflow by itself is only a container.
The actual business logic lives in its ordered steps:
Once Workflow Steps exist, we can build complete business processes that every module in KoreVity can execute consistently.
Now we build what actually makes a workflow useful.
A Workflow is only the blueprint.
The Workflow Steps define the journey.
Now the ERP knows exactly what to do.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: A Workflow Step is not a Task.
This is one of the most common ERP mistakes.
A Task is work performed by someone.
A Workflow Step is a stage in a business process.
The workflow only knows about the stage.

sections.title: A Workflow Step is a reusable stage within a workflow definition that specifies a unit of process logic, participant assignment, transition conditions, and execution behavior.
Purpose
paragraphs: Workflow Steps become the foundation for:

sections.title: Entry Condition
paragraphs: Only enters if condition is true.

sections.title: Business Rules
paragraphs: Parallel steps allowed only when explicitly enabled.

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: "Finance Review adds an average of 3.6 days. Consider running Finance and Legal reviews in parallel."
lists: Which step causes the biggest delays?

sections.title: Support Parallel Steps
paragraphs: Parallel execution dramatically reduces process time.

sections.title: Workflow Step as the Process Logic Hub
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: Workflow Step is not a task.
lists: The execution logic of a workflow.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: This is the same pattern we've consistently used throughout KoreVity:
That allows hundreds or thousands of workflow executions to run simultaneously from the same workflow definition without interfering with each other.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would add Step Outcomes as a future child entity rather than hardcoding transitions.
This creates a true workflow graph instead of forcing every workflow to be purely linear, enabling complex branching while keeping the step definition clean.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next entity should be Workflow Instance.
So far we've built the design of the workflow.
Now we need the runtime object that says:
"Purchase Order #PO-10458 is currently executing Workflow Version 3 and is waiting at Finance Approval."
That's the entity that brings the workflow engine to life.
This is where the Workflow Engine actually comes alive.
Everything we've built so far is a template.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: A Workflow Instance is not a Workflow.

sections.title: A Workflow Instance is the runtime execution of a workflow definition for a specific business entity, maintaining execution state, progress, participants, timing, and completion history.
Purpose
paragraphs: Workflow Instances become the foundation for:

sections.title: Responsibilities
paragraphs: It does not define the workflow.

sections.title: Business Rules
paragraphs: Only one active workflow instance of the same workflow per entity unless explicitly allowed.

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: AI becomes a workflow operations manager.
"17 purchase orders are currently waiting at Finance Approval for more than 48 hours."

sections.title: Support Parent–Child Workflow Instances
paragraphs: Each child is its own workflow instance.
The parent waits until all children finish.

sections.title: Workflow Instance as the Runtime Hub
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: Workflow Instance is not a workflow.
lists: The execution engine of business processes.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: We're now following the same pattern used throughout KoreVity:
That separation allows thousands of workflow executions to run concurrently while the workflow definitions remain stable and version-controlled.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I'd introduce a Correlation ID for workflow instances.
Every child workflow, notification, approval, and automation spawned during onboarding shares the same Correlation ID.
This makes debugging, monitoring, and AI analysis across complex business processes dramatically easier.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next entity should be Workflow Instance Step.
The Workflow Instance tells us where the process is.
The Workflow Instance Step tells us what actually happened at each step:
That completes the runtime execution model of the workflow engine before we build specialized entities like Approvals and Automation Rules.
This entity completes the runtime execution model.

sections.title: "Where is the process now?"
paragraphs: Then the Workflow Instance Step answers:

sections.title: "What happened at every step?"
paragraphs: This is one of the most valuable audit entities in the entire ERP.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: A Workflow Instance Step is not a Workflow Step.

sections.title: A Workflow Instance Step is the runtime execution record of a workflow step within a specific workflow instance, capturing assignments, actions, timing, outcomes, and audit history.
Purpose
paragraphs: Workflow Instance Steps become the foundation for:

sections.title: Responsibilities
paragraphs: It does not define the step.

sections.title: Assigned To
paragraphs: May differ from the template assignment.

sections.title: Business Rules
paragraphs: One execution per workflow step unless retries are enabled.

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: AI now has complete process visibility.
"Finance Approval averages 2.8 days while the target SLA is 1 day."
lists: Who has the highest approval backlog?

sections.title: Support Reassignment
paragraphs: The reassignment itself becomes part of the audit history.

sections.title: Workflow Instance Step as the Execution Hub
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: Workflow Instance Step is not a workflow definition.
lists: The execution history of business workflows.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: The runtime model is now complete.
This mirrors the same architecture used elsewhere in KoreVity:
That consistency makes the entire platform easier to understand, extend, and maintain.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: Rather than storing a single assignee, I'd support an Assignment History child entity in the future.
This preserves every routing decision without overwriting earlier assignments, giving auditors and AI complete visibility into how work moved through the organization.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next entity should be Approval.

Now we can create a specialized Approval entity that standardizes approval decisions across Purchase Orders, Leave Requests, Expenses, Contracts, Projects, HR actions, and every future module—without each module implementing approvals differently.
Now we build one of the most reused entities in the entire ERP.
Almost every business process eventually asks the same question:

sections.title: "Who approved this?"
paragraphs: Think about everything we've already designed.
If every module builds its own approval system...

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: An Approval is not a Workflow.
It is also not a Workflow Step.
A Workflow Step defines the stage.
An Approval records a person's decision.

sections.title: An Approval is the formal decision recorded by an authorized participant during the execution of a workflow, documenting authorization, rejection, delegation, comments, and decision timing.
Business Rules
paragraphs: One decision per approver per step.
Delegated approvals retain original approver history.

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: AI becomes an approval intelligence assistant.
"Purchase approvals assigned to Finance Team B exceed SLA 37% of the time."
lists: Which approvers cause the longest delays?

sections.title: Engineering Summary
lists: The approval foundation for the ERP.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Every approval anywhere in KoreVity now follows the exact same model.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I'd add an Approval Policy entity in a later phase instead of embedding approval requirements into workflows.
Workflows then reference policies instead of hardcoding approval logic, making organizational changes far easier.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next entity should be Business Rule.
Business Rules answer when, why, and under what conditions something should happen.
Business Rules become the decision engine that powers workflows, automation, AI recommendations, and future no-code process customization across the entire ERP.
Now we arrive at one of the most powerful entities in the entire ERP.
This is the entity that transforms KoreVity from:
lists: If purchase amount > $10,000 → require Finance Approval.
If leave exceeds 10 days → require HR approval.
If invoice is overdue by 30 days → notify Collections.
If inventory falls below reorder point → create Purchase Request.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: A Business Rule is not a Workflow.

sections.title: A declarative statement that evaluates business conditions and determines whether an action should occur.
paragraphs: The rule never performs the approval.
It decides whether approval is required.

sections.title: A Business Rule is a reusable declarative policy that evaluates one or more business conditions and produces a decision used by workflows, automation, validation, notifications, or other platform services.
Purpose
paragraphs: Business Rules become the foundation for:

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: This is where AI becomes extremely powerful.
"Three purchase approval rules overlap. They can be merged into one without changing business behavior."

sections.title: Business Rule as the Decision Hub
🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: We've now separated three concepts that many ERPs incorrectly combine.
This separation makes KoreVity extremely flexible:
Each layer has exactly one responsibility.
lists: Business policies can change without redesigning workflows.
Workflows can be reused across departments.
Approval history remains independent and fully auditable.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: Instead of storing a single expression, I'd model the rule as a tree of Rule Conditions in a future enhancement.
This allows non-technical administrators to build sophisticated rules visually without writing expressions, opening the door to a true no-code business rules engine.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next entity should be Automation Rule.
Business Rules determine what should happen.
Automation Rules determine what the system actually does when those conditions are met.
That completes the transition from decision engine to automation engine, making KoreVity capable of running business processes with minimal manual intervention.
This is where KoreVity stops being an ERP that guides users and becomes an ERP that works for users.
This is the heart of intelligent automation.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: An Automation Rule is not a Business Rule.
The business rule never starts the workflow.

sections.title: An Automation Rule is a reusable platform rule that performs one or more system actions when defined business conditions or events are satisfied.
Purpose
paragraphs: Automation Rules become the foundation for:

sections.title: Responsibilities
paragraphs: It does not decide business policy.

sections.title: Business Rule
paragraphs: Automation may depend on one or more rules.

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: "Invoice notifications execute synchronously and add 1.4 seconds to invoice creation. Consider asynchronous execution."

sections.title: One Rule Can Execute Multiple Actions
Automation Rule as the Action Hub
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: Automation Rule is not a business rule.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Notice the complete separation we've achieved.
Each layer has exactly one responsibility.
This architecture lets you change business policy, automation behavior, workflows, or approvals independently without affecting the others—a hallmark of mature enterprise platforms.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: Instead of storing actions directly inside the Automation Rule, I'd introduce a future Automation Action child entity.
Each action becomes independently configurable, reorderable, and reusable, making complex automation pipelines much easier to maintain.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next entity should be Notification.
Almost every automation eventually needs to communicate with someone:

A centralized Notification entity ensures every module uses the same messaging infrastructure instead of implementing its own, keeping communication consistent, auditable, and extensible across the entire KoreVity platform.
Now we build one of the most visible platform services in the entire ERP.
Every user expects the system to tell them:
A good notification system informs users at exactly the right time, through exactly the right channel.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: A Notification is not an Email.
It is not a Push Message.

sections.title: A business message generated by the platform.
A Notification is a platform-generated business communication informing one or more recipients about an event, workflow, automation, or system activity through one or more delivery channels.
Responsibilities
paragraphs: It does not send email directly.

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: "You have 17 unread notifications. Three require immediate action and two are overdue."

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Communication is now fully separated from automation.
This means the same automation can notify users through different channels depending on preferences, urgency, or organizational policy—without changing the automation itself.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: Rather than storing delivery results directly on the Notification, I'd introduce a future Notification Delivery child entity.
This lets each delivery channel have its own timestamps, retries, failures, and diagnostics while the Notification remains the single business message.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next entity should be Scheduled Job.
Not every automation is triggered by a user action.
A centralized Scheduled Job entity gives KoreVity a single scheduling engine that every module can use instead of building separate timers and background services.
Now we build the heartbeat of the ERP.
Most enterprise work doesn't happen because someone clicks a button.
Someone should not have to remember to do those things.
lists: On the first day of the month

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: A Scheduled Job is not an Automation Rule.

sections.title: A Scheduled Job is a reusable time-based execution definition that runs one or more platform actions according to a defined schedule, independent of user interaction.
Purpose
paragraphs: Scheduled Jobs become the foundation for:

sections.title: Responsibilities
paragraphs: It does not perform business logic itself.

sections.title: Schedule Expression
paragraphs: Store as schedule definition rather than hardcoding.

sections.title: Business Rules
paragraphs: Only one active execution unless concurrent execution is enabled.

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: "Nightly inventory synchronization overlaps with database backups. Moving it by 30 minutes will reduce contention."
lists: Which scheduled jobs fail most often?

sections.title: Jobs Should Not Contain Business Logic
Scheduled Job as the Time Engine
🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: We now have all three trigger models in the platform.
Every automated process in KoreVity will begin from one of these three trigger types.
That gives the platform a clean, consistent execution model.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I'd separate Scheduled Job from Job Execution.
This keeps the definition lightweight while allowing unlimited execution history, performance metrics, logs, retries, and diagnostics without bloating the main job record.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next entity should be Event Subscription.
Many things are triggered by events.

An Event Subscription entity allows any module—or even external systems—to react to these events without hardcoded dependencies, completing the event-driven architecture that will make KoreVity highly modular, extensible, and integration-friendly.
This is one of the biggest architectural upgrades we'll make.
Until now we've built an ERP.
Now we're building an event-driven platform.
Modern enterprise systems don't communicate by directly calling each other.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: An Event is not an Automation Rule.
An Event is not a Workflow.

sections.title: Something happened.
paragraphs: The Invoice module doesn't know any of these.

sections.title: An Event Subscription is a reusable registration that listens for one or more business events and invokes configured actions when those events occur.
Purpose
paragraphs: Event Subscriptions become the foundation for:

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: "The 'Invoice Paid' event triggers 14 independent automations. Three appear redundant and can be consolidated."
lists: Which events generate the most downstream activity?

sections.title: Publish–Subscribe Architecture
paragraphs: Every module depends on every other module.
Invoice doesn't know who is listening.

sections.title: Event Subscription as the Integration Hub
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: Event Subscription is not an event.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: This is arguably the most important scalability decision in the entire platform.
Instead of modules calling each other directly:
Every module is now loosely coupled.
This architecture is used in modern enterprise platforms because it minimizes dependencies while maximizing extensibility.
lists: New modules can be added without modifying existing ones.
AI can observe business events without changing business logic.
Performance scales far better because subscribers can execute asynchronously.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would introduce a future Business Event entity separate from Event Subscription.
That provides a permanent event log, enables event replay, supports debugging, and opens the door to full event sourcing if KoreVity ever needs it.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The final entity of this phase should be Process Template.
Right now we have all the individual building blocks:
A Process Template packages these together into a reusable business process such as:
That becomes the highest-level orchestration object and completes the Workflow & Business Process Automation phase with a clean, enterprise-grade process architecture.
A Process Instance would track the entire onboarding lifecycle across all those workflows, giving executives and AI a single end-to-end view of business process execution.

sections.title: My Recommendation for Phase 9
paragraphs: The natural next phase is Integration & Platform Services.
This would include capabilities such as:

At this point, KoreVity is a fully capable ERP internally. The next major step is enabling it to communicate securely and reliably with payroll providers, banks, e-commerce platforms, government systems, BI tools, AI services, and customer applications—turning KoreVity into an open enterprise platform rather than a closed application.
